- Workloads: short chat turns (avg 32 tokens), long chat turns (avg 320 tokens), prefix reuse scenario

Attachments: MAP_Plan_v2.pdf (pdf), nova_sample_workload.json (json)

Quick bench summary (preliminary) — ran on r-inference/open-chat-7B (fp16) and open-chat-7B-quant (int8) with Nova's sample traces. CSV attached (rdw_bench_results.csv). Raw logs are in the shared Drive link.

Test configuration (short):
- Hardware: single A100-equivalent GPU, baseline serving runtime v3.8.
- Sessions: 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 concurrent simulated websocket sessions, each streaming tokens as client types.
- Warm runs: pre-populated KV cache for prefix reuse; Cold runs: fresh process with empty KV.

Key results (median across 10 runs each):
- Short turns (avg 32 tokens) — FP16, Warm: TTFT p50 115ms, p95 210ms, p99 260ms. Cold: p50 220ms, p95 410ms, p99 620ms.
- Short turns — INT8, Warm: TTFT p50 135ms, p95 245ms, p99 320ms. Cold: p50 260ms, p95 490ms, p99 740ms.

Streaming per-token latencies (steady state, 1 token windows):
- FP16 Warm (1 session): p50 6ms, p95 18ms, p99 32ms.
- FP16 Warm (16 sessions): p50 8ms, p95 28ms, p99 52ms.
- INT8 Warm (1 session): p50 9ms, p95 25ms, p99 45ms.
- Cold runs show additional 80–250ms on TTFT due to model load + kv warmup.

Throughput: sustained tokens/sec per GPU (FP16): approx 850 tokens/s at 8 concurrent sessions (long-turn mixes reduce tokens/sec).

Notes and recommendations:
- With current config FP16 warm runs meet Nova's TTFT p95 target of <=220ms for short turns (p95 210ms). Cold starts exceed target; recommend session pinning or warm-on-demand for production.
- INT8 has cost benefits but higher p95; consider int8 for batch-heavy paths where TTFT SLO is relaxed.
- For streaming SLO (p99 <=40ms), FP16 warm at 1 session meets it; at 16 sessions we see p99 ~52ms. If pattern is highly concurrent interactivity, add a higher capacity lane or autoscale thresholds.

Attachments: rdw_bench_results.csv (summary), raw logs link in Drive.

Dev Patel
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Results & suggested close timeline — Nova Therapeutics MAP

Emily / Samir — sharing the consolidated outcomes and a proposed short close timeline. Summary attached and CSV included. Highlights:
- FP16 warm runs meet your TTFT p95 goal (210ms) for short turns. Cold-starts exceed it — see mitigations below.
- Streaming p99 token latency is within 40ms for single-session interactive flow, but crosses 40ms at 8–16 concurrent interactive sessions.

Recommended production mitigations (to include in MAP):
1) Session prewarm / KV pinning for top 10% of users to eliminate cold TTFT spikes.
2) Dedicated pool for interactive tier with autoscale triggers on token-latency p95 rising.
3) Use FP16 for interactive lanes; consider INT8 for lower-priority batch jobs.

Proposed close timeline:
- 6/03: Review results and agree on mitigations & SLOs (today) — DONE if you confirm via reply
- 6/07: Legal/procurement sign-off on redlines (Samir)
- 6/09: Start pilot deployment (Dev + Nova infra)
- 6/21: Full rollout to production lane (if pilot metrics valid)

Next steps for you: please confirm the timeline and whether you want Redwood to include the session-prewarm change in the initial deployment scope (we can include as an optional config in the Dedicated plan).
